title: Load done slices only when needed
lead: Commands that need only open work stop reading every done and retired slice file at load, so their cost stays flat as the roadmap grows.
findings_note: Go rewrite evaluation 2026-10-15; owner chose lazy mapping (a) 2026-10-16
boundary: **Not in this slice:** caching across processes; changes to the on-disk layout.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`store.load` reads every slice file into `State.slices` (`src/slicer/store.py:712-761`) for every command. With about 300 items the Go rewrite evaluation measured reads at 70-80 ms. Most of those slices are done, and the cost grows with every slice that lands. `render`, `check` and `verify` need every slice. `next`, `list`, `show ID`, `start`, `note` and most writes look up one or a few slices by id (`state.slices.get(item.id)` at `cli.py:1423`, `ops.py:1869` and the like) or test membership (`item.id in state.slices`, `cli.py:2889`).

**Decision (owner, 2026-10-16): option (a).** `State.slices` becomes a lazy mapping that reads a slice file on first access, keeping the dict interface every module uses. The rejected options were (b), an explicit `load(..., slices="open"|"all")` that each command chooses, and (c), waiting for a measured budget to be exceeded.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/store.py`:
  - `load` lists the slice folders (live, done, retired) into a map from filename stem to path, without reading any file.
  - A `LazySlices` class (a `MutableMapping[str, Slice]`) holds that map and a cache:
    - `get`, `[]` and `in` for one id read only that file, through the same `_from_dict` and `Slice.from_dict(boundary_marker=…)` path as today.
    - Iteration, `len`, `keys`, `values`, `items`, `dict(...)` and `copy` first load every file, then behave exactly as today's dict, keyed by each file's *contained* id.
    - If a file read on demand holds an id other than its filename stem, the mapping loads everything and rekeys by contained id, so `verify`'s "id disagrees with filename" report (`verify.py:206-209`) is unchanged.
    - Writes (`__setitem__`, `__delitem__`) go to the cache.
  - `State.slice_files` gets the same treatment, a lazy view over the same stem map, so `verify.py:209` still sees every path after a full load.
  - `store.py:391-393` (put a slice, with staging) and the staged save at `store.py:487` work on the mapping unchanged.
- `src/slicer/ops.py:2530-2531` and `:2595`: the import/promote draft copies `dict(state.slices)`. Make that a mapping copy that does not force a full load (a `LazySlices.copy()` sharing the stem map with its own cache), or record in the note why a full load there is acceptable.
- `src/slicer/tui.py:983`: the TUI reload assigns fresh mappings; check it keeps working with lazy ones.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`: the `State` contract and "what a change must not break", on when slice files are read and what that means for errors.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.
- `tests/test_store_lazy.py` (new) and a benchmark fixture builder in `tests/support.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Load_ManyDoneSlices_NextReadsNone`: with 2,000 done slices and 3 open ones, `next --json --lean` reads none of the done files (count calls to the slice reader).
- `test_Load_ShowDoneSlice_ReadsOnlyThatFile`: `show <done id>` returns it in full and reads exactly one slice file.
- `test_Load_Render_ByteIdenticalToEagerLoad`: `render` output on the legacy fixture and on this repo's own tree is byte-identical to the eager load (keep the eager path as a test-only reference, or compare against committed render output).
- `test_Load_FileIdDisagreesWithName_VerifyStillReports`: a file `s5.json` holding id `s6` is still reported by `verify` exactly as today.
- `test_Load_CorruptDoneSlice_CheckStillFails`: a damaged done slice still fails `check` and `verify` with `corrupt`, naming the file.
- `test_Load_CorruptDoneSlice_NextUnaffected`: the same damaged file does not stop `next`. This is a deliberate behaviour change: today every command fails at load. Record it in the CHANGELOG.
- `test_LazySlices_SetThenIterate_SeesNewSlice`: a slice added by `put` shows in a later full iteration, and so does a slice moved to done.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and the 2,000-slice fixture; watch them go red, and record `next --json --lean` timings on the fixture before the change.
2. Add `LazySlices` and the lazy `slice_files`, wire `load` to them, and fix the copy sites in `ops.py`.
3. Run every command's tests; then the full suite. Compare `render` on this repo before and after (`slicer check` must pass, with render byte-identical).
4. Mutation-check: make `get` load everything (the "reads none" test fails); drop the rekey on an id mismatch (the verify test fails).
5. ARCHITECTURE.md and CHANGELOG; put the before and after timings in the handoff note.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite.
- `slicer check` passes; `render` output is byte-identical before and after.
- The handoff note has `next --json --lean` timings on the 2,000-slice fixture and on this repo, before and after.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
